title: Life Between the Tides
objective: After this level you can describe the animals of the zone between high and low tide.
summary: The intertidal zone stacks into spray, high, middle and low bands. Each species lives where it can handle the mix of air, water, heat and waves.

cards.headline: Some rocky shores wear stripes.
cards.body: Walk out on the rocks at low tide and look back up the shore. The plants and animals sit in distinct horizontal layers, one above another, like shelves in a pantry. The tides drew most of the lines.

cards.headline: A home that floods on schedule
cards.body: The intertidal zone is the strip where the ocean meets the land, between high and low tide. Its middle floods and drains twice a day. Living here means surviving swings in moisture, temperature and saltiness, and taking a pounding from waves. The higher up the rock you live, the longer you spend in the air: the high zone is underwater only at high tide, so it's hotter and drier. Imagine a house that floods twice a day, then bakes in between.

cards.headline: Four floors of the shore
cards.body: From the top down: the spray zone is only splashed, except in extreme high tides and storms. The high zone, underwater only at high tide, is home to hardy barnacles, snails and limpets. The middle zone spends about equal time wet and dry; mussels, sea stars and anemones live here. The low zone is almost always underwater, uncovered only by the lowest spring tides, and it holds the greatest variety of life, because it suits creatures that can't take long in the air.

cards.headline: Who gets which floor
cards.body: Why such neat layers? Each species lives where it can handle the balance of air and water, and where predators and competitors for space and food let it. Barnacles can take long hours high and dry. Sea urchins stay down in the low zone, where the sea almost never leaves. Each stripe on the rock marks a line where the rules of survival change.

cards.headline: The shore: zoned
learned: Intertidal: between high and low tide
Four bands: spray, high, middle, low
Moisture, heat, salt and waves all change
Each species lives where it can cope

questions.prompt: Which band of a rocky shore sits highest, covered by the sea only in extreme high tides or storms?

options.label: The low zone
options.rationale: That's the lowest band, almost always underwater.

options.label: The middle zone
options.rationale: The middle zone is wet about half the time.

options.label: The high zone
options.rationale: The high zone is underwater at every high tide.

questions.explanation: The spray zone sits above the high tide line; spray dampens it, and only extreme high tides or storms cover it.

questions.prompt: Why does the low intertidal zone hold the greatest variety of life?

options.label: It gets the most sunlight
options.rationale: Sunlight is not the reason given.

options.label: Waves never reach down that far
It has no predators at all
options.rationale: Predators and competitors shape every zone.

questions.explanation: The low zone is out of the water only rarely, so it suits organisms that cannot tolerate air exposure for long.

questions.prompt: From Level 25: when does the low intertidal zone finally come out of the water?

options.label: At every low tide, twice a day
During neap tides at the quarter moons
options.rationale: Neap lows are a little higher, not lower.

options.label: Only during storms
options.rationale: Storms cover the spray zone; they don't uncover the low zone.

questions.explanation: The low zone is uncovered only during the lowest spring tides, which come when the Sun, Moon and Earth line up at new and full moon.
